title: I'm making a body-horror roguelike deckbuilder where your cards are rotting ingredients and your relics live inside your ribcage
author: _solereaper
selftext:
**Ossarium** – a body-horror roguelike deckbuilder I'm making solo in Godot 4.



Chips × Mult against a target, but your cards are ingredients and the hands are rituals: two bones for a Marrow Broth, organ–blood–organ in order for a Bloodstream. Meat rots every round you hold it – fewer Chips, more Mult – and if you let it go too far, it bursts and clogs your ribcage, where your relics live in a grid and care about their neighbours. Every boss breaks a rule.



Up front: solo project, I can't draw – art comes from my own local ComfyUI pipeline, sounds and narration are generated with ElevenLabs, and most of the code was written with an AI assistant. The idea, the direction and the decisions are mine.



What I'd love to hear:



\- Does "your ingredients rot in your hand" sound fun or just stressful?

\- Is the screen readable? I've stared at it for so long that I genuinely can't tell anymore.

\- Anything in the trailer that makes you go "wait, what am I looking at"?



Thanks for reading this far – be as blunt as you like.

  
P.S. looking for some testers.

comments.author: counterclockwisdom
comments.body:
It comes off as complicated and potentially convoluted? The text description doesn’t help, either. It is not clear what the 
draw/hook of this game is unless I am really only looking a more complicated Balatro.

And not to be too harsh, but it sounds like an idea AI would come up with to make “Balatro with a horror twist”. More complexity without making the game intrinsically more fun or interesting. And there are punchy little AI taglines under titles and on your video transitions, occupying space with nothing-filled flavor text with a bloated sense of importance. It looks exhausting to play or read or understand in this game.

The most important question that needs to be answered to players (and you) is __what makes this game fun to play__? What compelling experiences does it provide that players want? You game might have it, but it’s not immediately clear what it is. And the rest needs to be cut more and the actually fun part made front and center

1. “Your ingredients rot in your hand” doesn’t sound stressful unless it’s in real time. It sounds like a decently interesting and strategic core mechanic for a roguelite card game.

2. I can read it, but this trailer goes in too deep to start that I don’t know what I’m looking at, so my brain kind of shuts off. Maybe the interface will look simpler without the tutorializing text.

3. Yes. All I recognize is the skeleton of Balatro and some grid inventory on the right, and I could not figure out what the inventory on the right has to do with anything.
